question.problem:
The vector $a$ is directed horizontally to the left and has magnitude 
 $8$, while the vector $b$ is directed vertically up and has magnitude $6.$ Which of the following is a unit vector that is parallel to $a+b?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we have to find $a+b.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $a+b$ goes from the tail of $a$ to the head of $b:$   

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253719/assets/19a22ffd49677b2ff17b4c69908280dcfcf30695c63ae4bb6e4ab83441146194.png)

To find the unit vector corresponding to $a+b,$ we have to divide by the magnitude: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+b}{|a+b|}\end{aligned}
$$

 

To find the magnitude, first notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}{|a+b|}^{2} & ={|a|}^{2}+{|b|}^{2} \\  & ={8}^{2}+{6}^{2} \\  & =64+36 \\  & =100\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude is

$$
|a+b|=\sqrt{100}=10
$$

and the corresponding unit vector is 

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+b}{|a+b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}(a+b).\end{aligned}
$$
